newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to terminate CEPA power deal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to terminate CEPA power deal.

text.p: The Pakistani government has decided to terminate, by mutual agreement, a project of the Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA) to set up a thermal power plant, Water and Power Minister Nisar Ali Khan said on Tuesday.

The official APP news agency quoted Khan as telling the National Assembly (lower house of parliament) that a memorandum of understanding for the project in the southern province of Sindh was signed two years ago but no physical work had been carried out at the Keti Bundar site.
"The termination will be done through mutual agreement," Khan was quoted as saying.
"But we will renegotiate agreement (on the project) wherever possible through mutual agreement."
Under a June 1995 agreement, CEPA was to build eight 660-megwatt coal-based thermal power plants for a total cost of $5.5 billion in Sindh.

CEPA also planned to develop a 14-meter deep sea port at Keti Bundar, about 60 km (37 miles) west of the port city of Karachi, and set up a special industrial zone at the site at a total cost of $1 billion.
APP quoted Khan as saying that as far as the deep sea port was concerned "we will move forward under the commitments".
The port was to be developed in three years and ships with a cargo handling capacity of 70,000 tonnes could berth at the 14 jetties planned to be built.

Khan's statement follows a decision by the Economic Ccordination Committee of the cabinet earlier this month to set up a committee to renegotiate the deal with CEPA, in which Hopewell Holdings Ltd holds a 20 percent stake and U.S. power giant Southern Co 80 percent.
CEPA officials in Pakistan could not be immediately reached for comment.
